sections.h2: Where do you file a deed in Hocking County, Ohio?
sections.html:
The Hocking County Recorder sits on the first floor of the county courthouse at 1 East Main Street in Logan, OH 43138, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 949. The recorder's page lists 740-385-2031 for the office and 740-385-0377 for its fax.

Counter hours run Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., but recording has a shorter window, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Copy requests should be in by 3:30, and the research room closes to the public at 3:45. The office also posts a weather rule: under a Level 2 snow advisory it opens at 10 a.m., and under a Level 3 emergency it stays closed, so call before driving in from the Hocking Hills side of the county.

Records reach back to 1818, the year the county was organized, and the office has kept electronic indexes since January 1, 1992. Logan is the county seat and largest city, and the villages of Buchtel, Laurelville and Murray City file at the same counter.

sections.h2: What are the Hocking County recording fees?
sections.html:
The county prints its own fee sheet. Recording costs $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each added page, and that price includes a $5.00 restoration fee. The same sheet lists the other common charges.

Payments for recording can be made at the counter, and the recorder's page also links an online payment portal and a land records search. The office states that it records and maintains real estate records but cannot run title searches, give legal advice or prepare documents. Have the deed drafted by a title company or an attorney before you arrive.

sections.h2: What formatting standards apply to a Hocking County deed?
sections.html:
The county explains that House Bill 525 took effect July 1, 2009 and created the standards now found in section 317.114 of the Revised Code. A document that does not conform costs an extra $20.00. The county lists the requirements:

  • Computer type of at least 10 point.
  • Paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 and no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Black or blue ink only, and no highlighting.
  • One-inch margins on each side and at the bottom.
  • A three-inch top margin on page one, kept clear for the recorder, auditor and engineer, and a one-and-a-half-inch top margin on every later page.

The law does not reach court or taxing authority documents, plats, DD-214 discharges, state or federal documents, or papers signed before the effective date. Court papers are therefore outside the surcharge, while a deed you draft yourself is not.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Hocking County Recorder file?
sections.html:
The county posts a long list, and a seller's file may touch several items on it. Deeds include warranty, quit claim, survivorship and sheriff's deeds. Mortgage papers include releases, assumptions, assignments, subordinations and waivers of priority. The office also files certificates of transfer, affidavits, easements, leases, land contracts, plats, condominium records, powers of attorney and trusts.

Several categories matter at a sale. Liens on the list include mechanic's liens, notices of commencement, federal and personal tax liens, workers' compensation liens, unemployment compensation liens, Medicaid fraud liens and child support liens. A buyer's title company will search for these, and a seller who knows of one should say so early. The list also shows that annexations, street name changes, vacated streets and alleys, and zoning resolutions are recorded here, which can affect a rural lot's frontage.

sections.h2: What does the Hocking County Auditor handle on a transfer?
sections.html:
Before the deed is recorded, the buyer files a statement of value with the county auditor under section 319.202, and the seller pays the fee in section 319.54(G)(3): $1, or ten cents for each $100 or fraction of $100, whichever is greater. The county's auditor lists a conveyance fee calculator under its tools menu. It computes a figure for a sale price and parcel count, and it includes a parcel transfer fee.

The auditor's office, reached at 740-385-2127 on weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm, also decides what counts as short-term rental property. Its January 2026 message says short-term rentals have been separated from residential properties and valued on their market value as short-term rentals. An owner who sells a cabin near the state park should ask how the parcel is classified before quoting a tax figure to a buyer.

A transfer tax is optional for counties under section 322.02, with a cap of thirty cents per $100. Ask the auditor whether Hocking County levies it.

sections.h2: How do taxes and the land bank touch a Hocking County sale?
sections.html:
The Hocking County Treasurer's office is in the courthouse, Suite 201, at 740-385-3517. The treasurer's page announced that, because of recent legislation, the 2026 second-half collection date moved to August 7, 2026 for real estate and mobile homes. That date is in the past, so a seller who closed around it should confirm with the treasurer that both halves are settled.

The auditor's January 2026 message also describes new state laws signed December 19, 2025. House Bill 186 raises the owner occupancy credit from 2.5% toward 15.38% by tax year 2029 and phases out the 10% non-business credit, and House Bill 335 slows growth in inside millage to the rate of inflation. Most of that shows up on bills from 2027 on.

The county also runs a land bank. Its page says the bank acquires vacant, abandoned and tax-foreclosed properties, waives delinquent taxes on property it takes, and deed-restricts residential parcels to prevent nightly rentals. Owners of worthless or low-value parcels can offer them to the bank instead of leaving them to a tax foreclosure.

The land bank page also says the bank is governed by a five-member board that includes the county treasurer, two commissioners, the mayor of the largest municipality and one member with real estate experience. Residential houses it sells go to buyers who show a need for single-family housing and agree to owner-occupy.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Hocking County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau lists Hocking County at 27,512 people in July 2025, with 13,024 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a 78.8% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $186,400, median gross rent of $808 and median household income of $62,960. The mean commute is 30.3 minutes, the longest of the three counties in this part of Ohio that the Census table compares.

Roughly 70.6% of residents lived in rural areas in 2020, and part of the Wayne National Forest and Hocking Hills State Park lie in the county. The Hocking River drains about half the county, and Salt Creek drains much of the southwest.

Accommodation and food sales of about $89 million in 2022, the highest of the three counties, point to a visitor economy. A seller near the park should not assume a buyer wants a long-term home.

faqs.q: How much does the Hocking County Recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each additional page, which includes a $5.00 restoration fee. A nonconforming document costs another $20.00.

faqs.q: What are the recording hours in Hocking County?
faqs.a: Recording runs Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The office is open to the public until 4:00 p.m., and the research room closes at 3:45.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of a recorded deed by email?
faqs.a: Yes. Email copies cost $2.00 per page, and the recorder's page gives a copy-request email address. Requests should be submitted by 3:30 p.m., and copies printed in the office cost $1.00 per page.

faqs.q: Does Hocking County charge an Ohio conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Yes, through the auditor. Section 319.54(G)(3) sets $1, or ten cents per $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is greater. The auditor's calculator shows the figure with a parcel transfer fee.

faqs.q: Does the recorder check titles or write deeds?
faqs.a: No. The office states that it cannot perform title searches, give legal advice or prepare documents. Use a title company or attorney, then bring the signed deed in.
